chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who raised it to Abu Basir from Ali al-Sa'igh, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, the believer intercedes for his close friend, and that is known, except if he is a Nasibi. So if every sent prophet and every honored angel interceded for him, their intercession would not be accepted.

key_terms.نَاصِبِیّاً: Nasibi (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: Who is the exception to the rule of believer's intercession?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (a.s.) clarifies that while intercession (Shafa'ah) for a believer's close companion is a established reality, it is specifically negated for the Nasibi due to their enmity with the Ahl al-Bayt. This highlights the unique status of the Ahl al-Bayt in the economy of salvation, where even the collective intercession of all prophets and angels cannot compensate for the specific spiritual barrier of the Nasibi's hostility.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 21.  Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) says that a believer can surely intercede for his friend except a nasibi because even if all the prophets, messengers and honored angels intercede for a nasibi, their intercession will not be accepted.
